title: NY State Senate · District 11
area: Northeast Queens, including Flushing, Whitestone, Bayside, Fresh Meadows and College Point.

context.text: Incumbent Toby Ann Stavisky advanced from the Democratic primary without appearing on the ballot after two challengers withdrew or were disqualified; Pamela Michos advanced from the Republican and Conservative Party primaries without appearing on the ballot.

candidates.name: Toby Ann Stavisky
candidates.currentRole: NY State Senator, District 11 (since 1999; redistricted from District 16 to District 11 in 2023)

summary.text: Toby Ann Stavisky is the Democratic incumbent for NY State Senate District 11 in Queens. A former high school social studies teacher, she was first elected to the Senate in 1999 and is seeking re-election against Republican and Conservative Party candidate Pamela Michos. She chairs the Committee on Higher Education and serves as Vice President Pro Tempore of the Senate.

background.text: Born in New York, New York; graduated from the Bronx High School of Science.
Earned a B.A. from Syracuse University, where her Senate biography says she attended on an academic scholarship, and master's degrees from Queens College and Hunter College.
Worked as district manager for Northeast Queens for the 1980 U.S. Census, in the actuarial department of an insurance company, and as a social studies teacher in New York City high schools.
Her husband, Leonard Stavisky, a university professor, chaired the Assembly Education Committee and later served in the State Senate until his death in June 1999.
First elected to the State Senate on November 2, 1999, and re-elected thirteen times since, according to her Senate biography.
The first woman from Queens County elected to the New York State Senate, and the first woman to chair the Senate's Higher Education Committee.

Serves as Vice President Pro Tempore of the Senate and chairs the Committee on Higher Education. Also sits on the Education, Ethics and Internal Governance, Finance, Judiciary, Racing, Gaming and Wagering, and Women's Issues committees.
Serves as a trustee of the City University Construction Fund, a member of the Higher Education Capital Matching Grants Board, and treasurer of the Legislative Women's Caucus.
Lives in Whitestone and has one son, according to her Senate biography.

priorities.text: Supporting a teacher evaluation system that takes student test scores into account and raising the state's charter school cap, which she said would benefit New York schoolchildren, as part of New York's 2010 Race to the Top application.

positions.summary: Says she grew up in a rent-controlled apartment and joined other senators pushing for stronger rent laws, saying affordable housing is an investment in the state's communities and families.
positions.quote: I grew up in a rent controlled apartment on the Upper West Side of Manhattan, so I understand the importance of affordable housing.

positions.summary: As Senate Higher Education Committee chair, praised New York's 2010 Race to the Top application for including an increase in the state's charter school cap, saying the changes would benefit schoolchildren.
Co-sponsored a 2023 bill requiring anyone possessing a firearm to hold a firearms safety certificate.

record.text: Co-sponsored S1701 (2023), which would require persons possessing any firearm to hold a firearms safety certificate and establish an application and training process; remained in the Senate Codes Committee as of January 2024.

Chairs the Senate Committee on Higher Education; also serves as Vice President Pro Tempore of the Senate, Trustee of the City University Construction Fund, member of the Higher Education Capital Matching Grants Program Board, and Treasurer of the Legislative Women's Caucus. Also serves on the Education, Ethics and Internal Governance, Finance, Judiciary, Racing/Gaming/Wagering, and Women's Issues committees.

Sponsored S611A ("Emma's Law"), granting crime victims the right to be heard at sentencing in certain cases where a felony driving charge causing serious injury is pled down to a misdemeanor; passed the Senate unanimously 62–0 on May 7, 2026 and was pending in Assembly committee as of that date.

summary.text: Pamela Michos is the Republican and Conservative Party candidate for NY State Senate District 11 and is running for public office for the first time. A Whitestone native, she describes a career in banking, financial services and wealth management, and is PTA president of a Greek school in Flushing. She is running against incumbent Toby Ann Stavisky.

background.text: A Whitestone, Queens native of Greek (Kefalonian) descent, according to a National Herald report; an endorsing club describes her as a single mother and Greek Orthodox Christian.

According to her campaign website, she graduated from New York University's Steinhardt School, where she studied Nutrition and Food Studies with a concentration in Clinical Dietetics, and earned an Associate degree in Liberal Arts from Nassau Community College, graduating magna cum laude.
According to her campaign website, she developed health literacy programs for underserved communities in the Bronx and was recognized by NYC Health + Hospitals for her service.

According to her campaign website, she has nearly a decade of experience in banking, financial services and wealth management and nearly 14 years of executive leadership experience with publicly traded companies, and is a former small business owner. An endorsing club describes her as having "managed billions of dollars."
Serves as PTA president of the Stefanos and Areti Cherpelis Hellenic School of Saint Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in Flushing.

This is her first run for public office; she is running on the Republican and Conservative Party lines, and a campaign fundraiser was held in Bayside in September under the slogan "Protect the American Dream."

priorities.text: An endorsing club describes her as planning to redirect state spending on services for undocumented immigrants toward a down-payment assistance program for young families.
An endorsing club describes her as supporting expanded subsidized maternity leave and worker protections.
